Six peripherals give polling, pin stability, execution, experiment decisions, comparison evidence and output safeguards their primary explanatory locations. Workflow variants, numeric limits, retry mechanics and cleanup sequences have moved out of the overview. [M] means modular structure, including public/internal boundaries and dependencies; [C] means call flow; [O] means ownership/lifetime; [D] marks computational data dependencies, not another organizational layer.

The critique's adapter-scope issue is corrected: the entire execution expansion attaches to Run orchestration, while its adapter subtree owns only session behavior. Publication has a separate edge directly to the promotion node inside retain. Peripherals sit beside their relevant central branches, with no intervening diagram columns. Measured text bounds leave at least 24 columns on the left, 12 on the right, and four empty rows between stacked peripherals. All seven diagrams are connected; endpoints use 1-based raw lines. Schema, printable ASCII, endpoints and non-overlap were checked. Rendered connector routing remains unverified.

Corrections and qualifications from the pinned source: edited attempts rerun workflow stages rather than only the selected stage (evalRunService.ts:278-300, 441-443; experimentService.ts:188-219). Validation retries cover validator failures, not runtime exceptions (evalRunService.ts:654-668). The seed's late-response guarantee is scoped to usePolled cleanup, which does not abort its request (EvalsPage.tsx:71-97). Mixed terminal success becomes partial only after active cells are gone (evalRun.ts:94-99). Reconciled judgement run/cell links can be absent (judgementService.ts:31-35). Public method names are setArchived and deleteRun. Ordinary promotion requires a finished cell for a new request, whereas placement backfill requires a finished run; an existing matching receipt is returned before source revalidation (evalRunService.ts:122-175).

Additional source detail includes stage-only prompt hashing and merge ancestry (evalPromptService.ts:14, 131-164), omitted revision-parent boundaries in endpoint copies (compareSessionService.ts:32-42), runtime resource isolation and cache identity (agentContextEvalRuntime.ts:18-35), and exact planned-cell coverage plus exclusive experiment ownership of a judgement (experimentService.ts:58-99). These expand the seed without reproducing other points.

Evidence is restricted to the point definition and eight pinned source texts; the seed supplies the starting content. Previous output and critique were used only as review feedback. Textual point pointers use the supplied relationships: contexts, generation, canvas, changes and storage. The collection-wide suggestion to reconcile other points or link their diagram IDs cannot be substantiated from these inputs, so no such implementation claims or diagram targets are invented.
